answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks through exponentially escalating bonding: each successive identity one operator mints demands far more locked capital than the last. A single honest copper-colored node stays cheap, but a farm spinning up thousands pays a saffron-scaled fortune in foregone yield. Quartz-clean proofs let peers verify the curve, so concentrated stake—once exposed—is slashed in bulk, making mass impersonation ruinously expensive rather than merely tedious.
